chapter: Boyhood and the West End camps
title: Bands heard as a youth and king cake parties where bands got the mule
summary: He heard Chris Kelly, Punch, Rene, Celestin and white bands; at king cake parties hosts often skipped paying the band.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: sixty-three, sixty-four. Before you started playing, did you listen to many bands before

you ever touched a horn? Oh yeah, I heard quite a few Dixieland bands. In those days they had all these good colored bands around town. Chris Kelly, Punch, Rene, Papa Celestine, they were all young comers then, you know what I mean? And they all played a powerful lot of music. Buddy Petit played nice stuff those days. Punch, Sam Morgan, Chris Kelly. Oh and they had quite a few good white bands. Pansaline had a good white Dixieland band. Johnny Beisdorff was at his peak. He was playing the Tokyo Gardens out at the Spanish Fort and Papa Celestine had the original tuxedos right across from him, the tranchinas. He had a good outfit. What's a king cake party? King cake party, he used to give these parties where they have a little doll or pecan in the cake. And whoever got that pecan had to give a party the following week. It would start around, I think, January or February the 8th. And it would go on for a couple of three weeks, or maybe four weeks, until somebody had got the pecan and didn't throw a party. Then the king cake party automatically peed it out. And what would they have at these parties? Well they'd have a beer, whiskey, stuff to drink, and a band. Nine out of ten the band got mule, because those people didn't have a lot of money those days. They'd hire a band for around eighteen dollars. And Kid Punch would come out there and they'd get Punch or Rene or whoever was playing good and loaded. When it come for time to pay the band off, whoever drew the party was hard to find. They were gone.

Kid Punch and Rene, Sam Morgan, those fellas, they half expected to be mule. And these fellas, some of them would be nervous enough to hide two bands for the party, you know, let them buck one.
